original_question: The Fatou Set of a Polynomial Automorphism of C^2 . Let f be a polynomial automorphism of C^2 , and suppose that f is not conjugate to an elementary map. Let Omega be a connected component of the set of points where the forward iterates {f n : n = 1, 2, 3, ...} are locally bounded, which is the Fatou set of f . Let us suppose that Omega is periodic, i.e. f n Omega = Omega for some n 6= 0. Let us first consider the case in which Omega is recurrent, i.e. Omega contains a point whose orbit does not converge to ∂Omega. In this case Omega is either (a) a basin of attraction of a sink orbit, (b) the basin of attractin of a Siegel disk, or (c) the basin of a Herman ring. It is not hard to construct examples of (a) and (b). (i) Can case (c) occur? Nothing at all seems to be known about periodic domains which are not recurrent. (ii) If Omega is not recurrent, does there exist P ∈ ∂Omega such that limk→∞ f nk (Q) = P for all Q ∈ Omega? (iii) If Omega is not recurrent, does there exist P ∈ ∂Omega such that f n P = P , and one of the eigenvalues of DF (P ) is e2πip/q ?
target_in_paper: The dynamics-section problem-list entry titled "The Fatou Set of a Polynomial Automorphism of C^2," i.e. the Bedford–Smillie question about classifying periodic Fatou components of a non-elementary polynomial automorphism of C^2 into recurrent versus non-recurrent cases, with the unresolved recurrent Herman-ring case and the non-recurrent boundary-attractor/root-of-unity questions.
correct_elements: Your draft is already very close to the paper’s actual problem entry. It has the right ambient space (C^2), the right class of maps (polynomial automorphisms not conjugate to elementary maps), the right object (a periodic connected component of the forward-bounded/Fatou set), the recurrent versus non-recurrent dichotomy, the three recurrent possibilities (sink basin, Siegel-disk basin, Herman-ring basin), and the two non-recurrent questions about convergence to a boundary point and the presence of a neutral root-of-unity eigenvalue at a boundary periodic point.
missing_details: The periodic component should be normalized by passing to a positive return period m >= 1 with f^m(Omega) = Omega; then one should set F = f^m so that Omega is F-invariant.
This normalization is essential because the draft later asks about DF(P) even though F is never defined.
The period should be stated as a positive integer m >= 1, not merely n != 0.
The non-recurrent convergence question should be formulated for the return map F^k = f^{mk}, not for all iterates unless Omega is already invariant.
Recurrent should be stated in omega-limit-set language: there exists z in Omega whose omega-limit set is not contained in the boundary partial Omega.
The Herman-ring alternative should be identified as the basin of an invariant annulus on which the return map is conjugate to an irrational rotation.
In the boundary periodic-point question, the point should be fixed for the return map F, i.e. F(P) = P, equivalently f^m(P) = P.
The eigenvalue condition should explicitly say that one eigenvalue of DF(P) is a root of unity e^(2 pi i p/q), with integers p and q >= 1.
To make the question stand alone, it helps to say that Omega is a connected component of the set where the forward iterates are locally bounded, i.e. the Fatou set in the paper’s phrasing.
refined_question: Let f: C^2 -> C^2 be a polynomial automorphism that is not conjugate to an elementary map, and let Omega be a periodic connected component of the set of points near which the forward iterates {f^n}_{n>=1} are locally bounded. Choose m >= 1 such that f^m(Omega) = Omega, and set F = f^m, so that Omega is F-invariant. If Omega is recurrent, then the paper notes that Omega is known to be either the basin of an attracting fixed point of F, the basin of a Siegel disk, or the basin of a Herman ring; can the Herman-ring case actually occur? If Omega is non-recurrent, must Omega be a semi-parabolic basin in the following precise sense: does there exist a point P in partial Omega such that F(P) = P, F^k(Q) -> P for every Q in Omega, and one eigenvalue of DF(P) is a root of unity e^(2 pi i p/q)?
justification: The draft essentially reproduces the original problem-list entry, but it leaves one paper-critical point implicit: once Omega is only periodic, the natural object is the first-return map F = f^m on Omega. Making that replacement resolves the otherwise undefined notation DF(P), sharpens the quantifiers, and keeps the question exactly at the paper’s scope: recurrent components are already narrowed to sink/Siegel/Herman possibilities, and the unresolved issue in the non-recurrent case is whether every such periodic component is attracted to a boundary fixed point of the return map with a root-of-unity neutral eigenvalue.
